The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.
The stories below describe dated official notices. Read their original event dates and source context; they are not a claim that applications or seats remain available.

These rows retain the reporting year and programme category supplied by the source. They describe a past graduating cohort; do not transfer a category-wide median to every specialisation or an individual offer.

Choose a few programmes that match your subjects and learning interests. Keep separate notes for academic eligibility, recognition, practical facilities and the full cost of attendance. A better-looking campus image does not answer those questions.

The official degree page identifies demonstration farms, research plots and crop-protection teaching facilities. Its practical curriculum includes field diagnostics and rural interaction; these are programme descriptions rather than measured student outcomes.

ACAR’s Plant Protection section describes insect collections, microscopy and teaching equipment. These resources give a more specific view of practical agricultural learning than a campus-size statement alone.

The official department description connects crop-management teaching to laboratory analysis and farm management. Its course table includes practical crop production in kharif and rabi seasons, rainfed agriculture and soil-fertility subjects.

JSACAT describes experiential learning and RAWE, while the parent group reports village-based agricultural activities. A separate official laboratory page describes computer access and a language laboratory for listening, speaking, reading and writing practice.

The programme outline gives concrete examples of practical teaching: seed and sowing exercises, horticultural propagation, surveying and irrigation work. These are published curriculum components, not confirmation that every listed visit occurs for every cohort.

The TNAU 2024–25 directory places Pushkaram in the Veppangudi/Thiruvarangulam area of Pudukkottai district. A current teaching-farm, laboratory, hostel or transport inventory was not established, so the profile does not present an operational-facility list.

The campus gallery includes labelled sections for laboratories, agricultural fields, farm activity and industrial visits. A current facilities inventory and detailed participation records were not verified.

PAC’s official site lists agricultural teaching units, while its extension department describes rural engagement through RAWE and village appraisal. Confirm the current cohort’s fieldwork schedule and teaching-unit access.

TRIARD describes agricultural land used for practical teaching and a crop cafeteria. Its facilities page lists a college library, language laboratory, laboratories and residential arrangements, but includes older details that should be reconfirmed before making accommodation plans.

The official Agriculture Farm page provides separate sections for dairy, poultry, fishery, beekeeping, practical crop production and allied activities. These establish the farm’s published teaching areas, without proving current livestock numbers or student access hours.

The college describes departmental laboratories, a library with digital resources and agricultural land for practical work. The homepage also mentions experiential units and RAWEP village placements; detailed current participation requirements should be requested from the college.

The official farm page describes 74.8 acres: 43.9 at the main campus and 30.9 at Thokapalli. It lists 16 instructional units, including orchards, crop cafeterias, protected cultivation and a pest-and-disease-management module.

SKCAS’s departmental descriptions identify a horticultural garden with propagation structures and model orchards, and a soil-science teaching laboratory. Entomology material links final-year rural experience to crop-pest problems.

The Veterinary Clinical Complex describes clinical medicine, surgery and radiology, and gynaecology/obstetrics services. It is located at Mahal, about two kilometres from the main campus according to the college.

The official agriculture department describes laboratories across its major subject areas. Its archive documents practical and rural engagement, with dates ranging across earlier cohorts rather than a guaranteed current-year schedule.

The agriculture page describes a university field used for practice and lists field trips, study tours and projects. Specific crop acreage, laboratory capacities and residential arrangements were not verified from the agriculture-specific sources read.

The faculty page describes 13 laboratories, agronomic fields, a tractor and farm machinery. It also identifies a polyhouse, vermicompost unit, drip and sprinkler irrigation, and medicinal/aromatic plants. This is an undated institutional inventory, so applicants should check current access and teaching schedules.

The published agriculture outline includes hands-on subject modules and describes visits to research and agricultural institutions. This is curricular information, not a guarantee of a particular destination or visit for every student.

CU’s current institute list describes the wider academic campus. A programme-specific agriculture farm, laboratory inventory and field-training schedule were not verified. General university facilities are not substituted for evidence of agricultural teaching access.

The college publishes laboratory manuals in protected cultivation, machinery, soil-and-water conservation and related subjects. University navigation also identifies apiary, vermicompost and food-quality-control units; current student access and capacity should be checked.

The agronomy department reports practical training alongside classroom teaching. Its extension activities include workshops, field visits and demonstrations intended to connect university knowledge with farming practice.
University sustainability evidence describes 40 acres of agricultural land, apiculture and mushroom production. Its report associates farm output with campus kitchens and local food procurement.

The school identifies Dabok as its teaching location, around 18 kilometres from Udaipur in its introductory description. It also advertises professional workshops, industry visits and a university startup incubator.

The school’s official account identifies subject laboratories and an ecological farming centre. Its description links the centre to training in sustainable farming and mechanisation; it does not document an identical practical timetable for every cohort.

The faculty identifies horticulture, soil science, genetics and plant breeding, plant pathology, agronomy and agricultural engineering laboratories. It describes crop experiments and visits to institutions such as Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute.

The B.Sc. page describes laboratory experiments, research-farm activities and polyhouses alongside rural work and agro-industry attachment. These are programme components, not verified employment outcomes.

The checked university pages establish the agriculture faculty and Udaipur contact location. They did not provide a sufficiently detailed, dated inventory of agricultural farms or laboratories to reproduce here.

The school describes instructional and research farmland, polyhouses, mist chambers and research plots. Its brochure additionally identifies experiential-learning modules, an agrometeorological observatory and an automatic weather station.

SGVU’s school page identifies instructional farms and protected-cultivation units. A separate school account describes farmer-student and farmer-faculty interactions on campus and in an adopted village.

The school’s dated event feed records a Pusa Krishi Vigyan Mela visit in February 2026 and sessions on water-use efficiency and soil quality later that year. A current inventory of dedicated farms and laboratory equipment was not verified.

The course page names a polyhouse, weather station, apiary, mushroom unit, nursery, orchard, vermicompost unit and biogas plant. The school page gives conflicting farm-area figures, so no acreage is presented as settled.

VAIAL describes agricultural and horticultural land, teaching and research laboratories, gardens, composting units, irrigation and machinery. Its events list records farmer-facing training as well as student and research activities.

The college’s 2023 self-study report identifies practicals, field visits, experiential learning, rural work experience and educational tours. Its 2024-25 institutional brochure also describes departmental laboratories and agricultural GIS training.

The faculty identifies an irrigated research farm and greenhouse, together with agricultural implements and a food-processing training centre. Farm experiments and demonstrations are described as outdoor teaching resources.

The school describes two instructional farms and an orchard at Bandhuguda. Its facility account names irrigation, a crop cafeteria, research blocks, mushroom, azolla and vermicompost units, and farm machinery.

The syllabus places Rural Agricultural Work Experience and Agro-Industrial Attachment in the seventh semester. Its final-semester list includes practical enterprise modules; the checked farm webpage itself contains no detailed facility inventory.

The school describes a farm-centred teaching approach. Its 2023 brochure identifies soil science, agricultural chemistry, animal-science and farm learning resources; this historical inventory needs current operational confirmation.

The faculty describes an agriculture farm with irrigation for technical training. Its account also identifies classrooms, laboratories, library facilities and separate boys’ and girls’ hostels; its undated hostel price is not treated as current.
The school names subject laboratories across crop, soil, animal and allied fields. Its RAWE and industry-attachment account describes work outside the classroom with farm and industry communities.

The faculty self-study report identifies a museum used for agricultural identification teaching and farmer training. It also describes postgraduate agronomy and entomology laboratories, with research-farm resources for crop experiments.
The course page identifies experimental fields, crop laboratories and farm machinery for teaching. The older school brochure additionally describes production demonstrations.
Agriculture uses research farms and laboratories, while fisheries has its own aquaculture teaching resources documented in the 2022 regulations.
The school identifies teaching spaces spanning crop production, livestock and the handling of harvested produce.
IIAST’s farm page distinguishes practical crop production, experiential learning and processing activity across separate units.
The official directory verifies the Etcherla location, but a college-specific inventory of farms and teaching laboratories was not accessible during this review.
The university disclosure index identifies common facilities and student services. A verifiable current inventory of agriculture farms and laboratories was not available in the pages read.
GLA’s agriculture pages identify practical crop work and subject laboratories within the faculty’s teaching approach.
The facilities page identifies a library with text and reference resources and internet access. A November 2021 government report records inauguration of a new administrative building.
SOA’s 2026 village attachment report documents supervised community and field activity. Its research agreement also describes shared instrumentation and library access for eligible researchers.
The agriculture faculty documents teaching and research resources across production, protection and resource management.
ICAR’s 21 August 2025 report describes an agriculture student visit to KVK Namsai at Momong. It supports external practical exposure rather than a claim about ownership of the KVK facilities.
The course page identifies instructional farm and horticulture resources, and explicitly describes Student READY learning components.

The school describes experiential learning, rural attachment, industry training, skills work and projects. A detailed current laboratory inventory could not be verified from the linked pages. A readable official school inventory identifies genetics/plant-breeding, plant-pathology, horticulture and agronomy equipment. Confirm present access and practical schedules with the department.
The brochure identifies an instructional farm and laboratory resources; the programme pages identify agronomy, crop protection and other subject spaces.
The university’s 2026 notices identify precision-farming and smart-agriculture project activity. A current programme-level facility and attachment inventory remains to be confirmed.
RNBGU’s procedure describes application, documents, aptitude testing, committee review and an offer specifying payment and reporting requirements.

The Plant Pathology department’s September 2022 account describes research work at the college’s Pili Kothi Farm and in its laboratory, with supervised investigations in field and laboratory conditions. These are documented departmental resources; their current allocation should be confirmed with the college.
